title: Smoke
description: Smoke is combustion particles with a source, a direction, and enough density to turn a room's air into a volume the light can strike. Unlike weather fog, it has a chimney, a cigarette, a tire, or a battlefield; backlight carves it into shafts and swirls.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A practical lamp becomes a wedge through grey air. A drag on a cigarette writes a ribbon.
Photograph the air of a room. The walls were always there; now the air is too.
Use it when volume should be visible indoors or when a battle, a chimney, or a club must have a source. It is the wrong tool when the veil is weather with no fire (Fog, Mist).
It is the wrong tool when the white stuff rises off a manhole because water met cold air: that is Steam. Without a key or backlight, smoke is only a smell.
Front-filling a room with unlit smoke turns faces to mud.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Pick a source and a particle (cigarette, incense, oil, battlefield pot). Control air currents so ribbons have direction.
Light from the side or behind so the volume renders; use a hard beam if you want shafts (Volumetric Light). Keep some clean path to the face.
Prompt: smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it, volume in the room.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for apartments, temples, engine rooms, aftermath. Do not use it as a default 'atmosphere' pass on a sunny kitchen.
If the beat is stillness in a closed parlor, Dust Motes in a shaft may be enough.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Atmospheric Haze in the distance is aerial perspective. A hazer used to fill a stage is a cousin of smoke but without a story source; still light it as volume.
Fog is wet weather. Steam is water vapor from heat, white, rising, condensing.
Dust Motes are discrete specks in a beam, not a ribbon.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: In the Mood for Love lets cigarette ribbons occupy cramped rooms. Blade Runner fills interiors so shafts and practicals have air to hit.
Apocalypse Now makes battle and jungle air into volume. Give smoke a source and a light, not a generic grey.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Fog (no source) or unlit fill that dirties skin. The tell: no chimney or cigarette, lamps without shafts, a muddy key.
The fix: a visible source, side or back light, a clean path to the eyes.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Smoke in film?
Smoke is airborne combustion particles from a source, dense enough that light can carve the room's air into volume. It has direction, swirls, and a reason to exist.
Smoke vs Atmospheric Haze
Haze pales distant planes over kilometers. Smoke occupies a room or a battlefield and needs a source and a sculpting light. One is distance; the other is volume you could walk through.
When should I use Smoke?
Use it to photograph a room's air, a chimney, a cigarette, a battle. Do not use it as weather, and do not fill a face with unlit particles.
How do I prompt Smoke for AI image or video?
Name source and lighting. Example: smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it. Demand a readable face and visible volume, not a grey grade.
